_comment: The mechanical sweep for this run's excerpts. Applied by parse.py --redact on the
way into the manifest, so the record check.py matches quotations against and the
record in this folder are the same swept record.
The M4 intake cleared this window and named only database identifiers and revenue
figures as the hazards, both of them outside the window. Neither is in this folder.
These two rules cover a category the intake did not anticipate: the window carries
a personal name, shipped as the default value of a configuration constant, and the
platform identifier of a real channel, twice, inside a file path. This repository is
public under a pseudonymous account, so shipping those would have linked the account
to the person. Redacting them is stricter than the ruling, not looser. Neither is
cited anywhere in the report, so nothing in the finding depends on them.
Note on how the first rule is written. A sweep rule that names its target as a
literal republishes the string it exists to remove — the rules file ships in the
same public repository as the manifest, and is just as greppable. So this rule
matches the surrounding syntax instead: the quoted default in the assignment. The
rules file therefore contains no personal name. Run 2's handle rule does spell its
target, and that is deliberate rather than inconsistent: the account handle is the
owner of this repository's own URL and is public whatever this file says, whereas
the name appears nowhere else in the repo.
Added by the M4 recovery session, 2026-08-08. Flagged for the human's final read:
see runs/01-too-complex-too-fast/run-notes.md and the M4 handover.
